title: Meeting Management
overview: Meetings are essential for coordination, decision making, problem solving, planning, and communication, yet poorly managed meetings can consume significant time without producing clear outcomes. Effective meeting management requires more than arranging a time and inviting participants; it requires clear objectives, appropriate preparation, structured facilitation, disciplined participation, accurate documentation, and consistent follow-up.

This course provides participants with the practical skills required to plan, organize, conduct, and follow up productive meetings. Participants will learn how to determine whether a meeting is necessary, define its purpose and expected outcomes, select the right participants, prepare focused agendas, manage time and discussion, encourage useful participation, handle difficult behaviors, and guide the group toward decisions and actions.

The program also covers meeting roles, facilitation techniques, decision-making methods, virtual and hybrid meeting practices, minutes and action tracking, and post-meeting evaluation. Through simulations and practical exercises, participants will develop a structured approach that makes meetings more focused, participative, accountable, and results-oriented.
audience: Managers, supervisors, team leaders, project managers, coordinators, executive secretaries, administrative professionals, committee members, meeting facilitators, and employees who organize, chair, participate in, document, or follow up business meetings.
methodology: The course uses an interactive and practice-oriented methodology combining short presentations, meeting-planning exercises, agenda-development activities, case studies, facilitation simulations, role plays, decision-making exercises, participant-management scenarios, meeting-minute analysis, action-tracking exercises, and structured feedback. Participants will plan and conduct simulated meetings and evaluate their effectiveness against practical meeting-management criteria.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Determine when a meeting is necessary and define clear meeting objectives and expected outcomes.
Select appropriate participants, roles, formats, and logistical arrangements.
Prepare focused agendas and supporting materials that enable effective discussion.
Open, facilitate, and close meetings in a structured and professional manner.
Manage meeting time while maintaining focus on priorities and outcomes.
Encourage balanced participation and manage dominant, silent, disruptive, or off-topic behavior.
Use practical methods to support problem solving, discussion, and group decision making.
Handle disagreement and conflict constructively during meetings.
Apply effective practices to virtual and hybrid meetings.
Document decisions and action items clearly and follow them through to completion.
Evaluate meeting effectiveness and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
